title: Startup security baseline
description: A pragmatic local-first baseline for personal and small-team software projects.

items.title: Enable MFA on core accounts
items.why: Email, source control, registrars, and payment tools are high-leverage takeover targets.
items.action: Enable app-based or hardware-key MFA for email, GitHub, domain registrar, hosting, and payment accounts.
items.evidence: Record account names reviewed and MFA method category; do not store backup codes here.

items.title: Move credentials into a password manager
items.why: Central inventory reduces password reuse and makes offboarding/recovery safer.
items.action: Create or review vault entries for every critical tool and remove passwords from notes, chats, and repos.
items.evidence: Vault coverage checklist by tool name only.

items.title: Document account recovery paths
items.why: Recovery weaknesses can bypass strong day-to-day controls.
items.action: For each critical account, document recovery email/phone ownership, admin backups, and registrar lock status.
items.evidence: Recovery owner and last-reviewed date per service; no secrets.

items.title: Run a small backup restore drill
items.why: Backups only matter if restore works under pressure.
items.action: Restore one representative database/export/file from backup into a safe test location and record the steps.
items.evidence: Restore date, dataset label, and time-to-restore.

items.title: Check repositories for committed secrets
items.why: Leaked tokens in git history are common and often long-lived.
items.action: Run a local secret scanner or GitHub secret scanning review, then rotate anything suspicious outside this plan.
items.evidence: Scanner used, repos checked, and rotation tickets opened.

items.title: Harden primary work device
items.why: A lost or compromised laptop can expose source, sessions, and customer data.
items.action: Confirm disk encryption, automatic updates, screen lock, malware protection, and separate admin/day-to-day use where practical.

items.title: Create an incident contact card
items.why: Clear first steps reduce panic during account takeover, outage, or data exposure.
items.action: Write who to contact, where status updates go, and which systems to preserve before changing anything.
items.evidence: Link or path to the incident card.
